messages:
From: Lisa Hammond <lisa.hammond@clearwater.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@clearwater.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 07:48:12 -0400
Subject: Immediate: degraded response latency and truncation from Redwood inference

Hi Lukas —

We started seeing widespread delays and truncated responses from the Redwood endpoint backing our customer chat flows starting around 06:40 ET. Symptoms: 60-90s response latency for text-generation calls, and on ~25% of requests the stream cuts off at token ~120 (clients see an abrupt end). This is happening across multiple models and both our prod+staging keys.

I've attached a short log snippet with two representative request_ids (2028-06-12T06:42:31Z/req-99a and 2028-06-12T06:51:07Z/req-101b). Our ops team is paused on deployment until we hear the status — impact is customer-visible and affecting SLAs.

Can you confirm you see this on your side and provide an ETA for a mitigation? If helpful we can open a phone bridge.

Attachments: log-snippet-0612.txt (text)

Thanks,
Lisa Hammond
Head of Platform Operations
Clearwater Financial

Hi Lisa — thanks for the flag and the sample IDs. We see the same error pattern in our edge metrics for your tenant and have an active incident (INC-4821) assigned.

Immediate steps we've taken:
- Degraded requests were routed to warm fallback nodes to keep responses flowing (short-term mitigation).
- We've pulled the two request IDs you sent into a focused trace and handed logs to infra.

Request to you: can you share one or two additional request ids and an example prompt that reproduces truncation? That will speed debugging.

I'll keep this thread for customer communication; Hannah is taking lead on the engineering RCA and Marissa will coordinate any contract/SLA communications. We do have a temporary mitigation in place but I want to be transparent about next steps and a timeline.

Proposed cadence: I'll send an engineering summary within 24 hours and a full RCA + action plan within 48 hours. If you prefer a quick call, I'm available 11:30–12:30 ET today.

Best,
Lukas Meyer
Senior Solutions Engineer

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 08:25:40 -0400
Subject: Internal: Clearwater incident — preliminary RCA and mitigation plan

On Tue, Jun 12, 2028 at 9:12 AM Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Lisa — thanks for the flag and the sample IDs. We see the same error pattern...

Team — quick technical summary and recommended actions for the customer-facing RCA. This is a concise view we can share in final form with Clearwater.

Timeline (UTC/ET rough):
- 2028-06-12 10:35 UTC (06:35 ET): First elevated error rate observed in routing service for batch handler A.
- 2028-06-12 10:40 UTC: Autoscaler added capacity; warm fallback nodes enabled to reduce tail latency.
- 2028-06-12 10:41 UTC: A race between our KV-cache eviction routine and an experimental continuous-batching fast-path caused stale cache entries to be used; downstream serializer hit a truncation branch when an expected token length header was missing.
- 2028-06-12 10:44 UTC: Partial responses and increased connection resets detected; mitigation applied (disabled experimental fast-path).
- 2028-06-12 11:10 UTC: Patch built to fix eviction ordering and additional validation added for token-length header; smoke tests passing.

Root cause (short):
- A timing window created by a new optimization (continuous-batching fast-path) allowed a stale KV-cache pointer to be referenced before the eviction handler completed. That sequence led to a malformed streaming header hitting the serializer, which produced early termination in ~25% of affected flows.

Customer impact:
- Intermittent high latency (60–90s) for affected batches; ~25% of requests experienced truncated streams. Impact window ~06:35–07:10 ET, small percentage of requests persisted at lower volume through 07:30 ET.

Immediate corrective actions (we've completed):
- Disabled experimental fast-path routing at 10:44 UTC. (Owner: Hannah)
- Deployed validation for token-length header to cause safe fallback rather than truncation (Owner: Dylan).
- Scoped autoscaler tuning reverted to previous stable thresholds (Owner: Infra).

Agreed follow-ups (customer-facing commitments):
1) Formal RCA document with timeline and remediation artifacts by EOD 2028-06-14. (Owner: Lukas / Hannah)
2) Patch to the KV-cache eviction ordering landed and can be staged to customer-dedicated pools for verification by 2028-06-15. (Owner: Dylan)
3) Post-deployment verification plan and a 72-hour monitoring window; we'll share SLOs and logs. (Owner: Marissa)
4) A short exec summary and credit proposal for Clearwater ops impact; Marissa will coordinate with Revenue. (Owner: Marissa)

Notes: we should keep the customer message crisp, emphasize what we fixed, when it happened, and how we'll prevent recurrence. Attach the code diff and the verification checklist.

Hannah
Principal Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Hammond <lisa.hammond@clearwater.com>, Clearwater Engineering <eng@clearwater.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 10:00:00 -0400
Subject: Post-incident summary, RCA, and verification plan — Clearwater impact 2028-06-12

Hi Lisa / Clearwater team —

Thanks again for your patience while we investigated. Below is a concise customer-facing summary of what happened, what we changed, and the verification steps we will perform with you. I've attached the full RCA PDF and the patch diff for transparency.

What happened (summary)
- Between ~06:35–07:10 ET on 2028-06-12, an experimental routing optimization (continuous-batching fast-path) interacted with a KV-cache eviction ordering bug. That created windows where stale cache pointers could be dereferenced, which sometimes produced a malformed streaming header that led to truncated responses.

Customer impact
- Approx. 25% of requests hitting the affected batches returned truncated streams; a larger set saw elevated tail latency (60–90s). The observable impact to Clearwater endpoints was concentrated in the window above.

What we changed (actions completed)
- Disabled the experimental fast-path routing during the outage to restore normal routing behavior.
- Deployed a validation check in the serializer to detect malformed token-length headers and trigger a safe fallback, preventing truncation.
- Fixed the eviction-ordering bug (patch attached as kvcache-patch.diff).

Planned verification and timeline
- 2028-06-14: Deliverables — full RCA PDF, code diff, and verification checklist (attached).
- 2028-06-15: Stage the patch to a Clearwater-dedicated pool; run smoke and synthetic load tests. (Owner: Dylan)
- 2028-06-15 to 2028-06-18: 72-hour monitoring window with daily health reports and access to token-level traces. (Owner: Marissa)

Compensation and next steps
- Marissa will follow up today with a proposed operational credit to offset customer impact and coordinate any contractual adjustments.

Attachments included
- clearwater-rca-20280614.pdf (full timeline, logs, and mitigations)
- kvcache-patch.diff (code-level change)
- log-snippet-0612.txt (customer-submitted sample)

Ask for you
- Please confirm a replication time for the staged rollout (we propose 09:00 ET on 2028-06-15) and whether you'd like Redwood engineers on the verification call.

If you prefer a quick technical review before the staged rollout, Hannah and I can join a 30-minute call tomorrow morning ET.

Sincerely,
Lukas Meyer
Senior Solutions Engineer
